readout_other: tactile-evoked potentials; multi-unit activity in S1 and POm with optogenetic tagging
direction_notes: High PRF, high duty cycle and high pressure (3 kHz, 60%, 163 kPa) increased the tactile-evoked N22 and POm RSU response; low PRF, low duty cycle and low pressure (30 Hz, 0.6%, 98 kPa) decreased it.
safety_notes: Temperature rise was measured during 500 consecutive tFUS trials (Table 1).

exposures.label: tFUS to S1 during hind-paw vibration

device.manufacturer: Sonic Concepts, Inc., Bothell, WA, USA
device.model: H276 128-element random array; driven by Verasonics Vantage 128

timing.protocol_description: Inter-sonication interval 2.5 s with 10% jitter; ultrasound duration 100 ms with tactile stimulation or 67 ms tFUS only; 250 trials per recording with tactile stimulation, 500 tFUS only; 30 Hz/0.6% and 3 kHz/60% each at low and high pressure, randomised order.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Vibration-tactile stimulation reliably evoked responses in both S1 and POm, as evidenced by clear tactile-evoked potentials (TEPs; Fig. 2A, N = 34 rats).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: The customized 128-element random array ultrasound transducer H276 (f<sub>0</sub>: 1.5 MHz, -3 dB axial specificity: 1.36 mm and lateral specificity: 0.46 mm, manufactured by Sonic Concepts, Inc., Bothell, WA, USA) was used.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.pressure_kpa: To mimic the in-vivo experimental setup, a rat skull sample was placed in degassed water, with the transducer placed vertically over the skull and the hydrophone measuring the ultrasound pressure beneath the skull. The peak-to-peak in-situ ultrasound pressure magnitude with beam steering was 98 kPa for the low-pressure level (Fig. 1C) and 163 kPa for the high-pressure level (Fig. 1D) and spatial-peak temporal average (I<sub>SPTA</sub>) was 32.76 $\mathrm { \ m W / c m ^ { 2 } }$ and 54.49 $\mathrm { \ m W / c m ^ { 2 } }$ respectively with 1500 Hz PRF, 30% DC and 67 ms UD. All tFUS parameters used in this study are summarized in Table 1.

flags.reason: Peak-to-peak pressure measured with a hydrophone beneath an ex vivo rat skull in water, not in the brain of the experimental animals; pressures 98 and 163 kPa.
The text gives Ispta 32.76 and 54.49 mW/cm2 for the 1500 Hz, 30% DC condition only; the table lists other values by condition. Converted from mW/cm2 to W/cm2.
Isppa (109.2 and 181.63 mW/cm2) is taken from Table 1 with no domain stated; converted to W/cm2.
Figure legend says pulse duration was calculated from PRF and DC; no value stated, so not recorded.
Text and Table 1 also include a 30 Hz/60% and 3 kHz/0.6% condition, and 1500 Hz/30% appears in Table 1 and the in situ sentence; list is of PRFs seen.
100 ms with vibration; 67 ms for tFUS only.
No sham ultrasound; tactile stimulation alone served as the comparison within the same animals.
Discussion argues auditory confound is unlikely citing prior work; no control in this study.
N = 34 rats for tactile responses; virus groups N = 10, 12, 12 (sum 34). Not all rats received every tFUS condition.
